current.text: His back looks fine for now. He looked good in the early preseason games, and reports said he was in good shape this summer.
Experts are only worried about the back if it flares up again. One expert says he looks much better than last season.
His back flared up again and again last season. He was effective in only about half of his games. He barely contested shots and blocked very little.
He is the projected starting center for Toronto and the only seven-footer on the roster.
Toronto's expected closing five is a small, switchable group with Murray-Boyles at center, not Poeltl. That can cut his minutes late in close games.
Experts see him as good value around pick 100 to 105 (rounds 9 to 10). In other mocks he went around pick 130, which one expert called a great pick, and for 4 USD in an auction mock.
If he plays 28 minutes and the back caused his drop in blocks, he is an easy top 70 pick.
He shot 70% from the field last season on low volume. An expert does not think that 70% will last.
He turned only 35% of his deflections into steals last season, so his steals are likely to go up.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games, or 56 to 57 if Kawhi Leonard plays 75 games.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, and three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He is an elite finisher. He makes almost all of his shots at the rim, and his FG% on real volume lifts a team's FG% clearly.
His free throw shooting has improved steadily from around 52%. It is still low at about 62% and hurts FT%.
He has lost a step on defense and is not an elite rim protector.
He has a history of back flare-ups and has not played 60 games in any of the last three seasons.

note: Yahoo and ESPN value him at only 1 to 2 USD (rank about 117), while experts take him around pick 100 and our league paid 15 USD last season. He is a cheap starting center who helps FG% and rebounds and fits punt 3PM builds, so a bid of a few USD is fair. In the first weeks, check his minutes (28 is the target), whether his blocks come back toward 1.2 to 1.5 a game, and any new back flare-up.
